summary: Open tools for computer-use agents: desktops for AI to operate, local VMs, a desktop automation driver and benchmarks.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Cua provides the computers and automation tools for AI agents that use desktops. It includes Cua Spaces (a desktop app that gives agents full desktops as VMs or images), Cua Driver for desktop automation, Lume for local macOS VMs, an SDK and CLI, small CUA-S1 decision models and Cua Bench for tasks.
sixtySeconds.problem: Letting an agent use a real computer safely needs isolated desktops, automation drivers and ways to test. Cua packages these pieces.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for cross-OS sandboxes, a shared multiplayer desktop with agents, and benchmarks, bringing your own agent and model.
requirements: macOS 26+ for Cua Spaces, or macOS/Linux/Windows for the CLI

overview: Install with the script on macOS or Linux, or the PowerShell script on Windows; on macOS it installs the Cua Spaces app plus the cua CLI. A signed .dmg is also available.

Spaces gives each agent a desktop (a local macOS VM or a Linux image) and lets you move a signed-in app into a Space after you approve. You and agents can work on the same desktop with separate cursors.
Spaces is free for individuals, with Pro at $18 a month and Teams at $30 per seat a month, per the README. The repo is MIT licensed; the Spaces app is source-available under FSL-1.1-MIT.
limitations: Paid plans for Pro and Teams
